Verdict: **PASS for the bounded pure naming policy**. No blocking UX findings.
This is a static review; it does not certify runtime checks, an authoritative
import producer, tree publication, or Android Studio UI completion.

## Behavior checked

- `Unavailable` produces a typed error rather than inventing a non-Gradle
  identity or interpreting an uncaptured getter as null. Captured `NotGradle`
  follows the imported-name fallback. `None` inside a Gradle capture explicitly
  means a getter reported null.
- Source-set modules resolve the final colon suffix before the root/nonroot
  project rule. Missing IDs and IDs without a colon use the imported name;
  a trailing colon gives an empty label. This matches pinned
  `GradleModuleSystem.kt:646–659` and
  `GradleProjectResolverUtil.java:531–540`.
- Other Gradle modules keep the entire reported external ID when project/root
  paths compare equal; otherwise they use the final colon component. Two
  reported null paths compare equal, one null does not, and no path, case,
  whitespace, Unicode, or filesystem normalization is introduced. The behavior
  matches `StringUtilRt.equal:21–40` and `getShortName:242–248`.
- Missing IDs trigger the imported-name fallback. Empty IDs and empty suffixes
  remain empty: the pinned Kotlin Elvis fallback replaces null, not empty.
  The Rust policy does not silently turn these inputs into a folder or project
  path label.
- Display names, holder-group display names, and sort names remain separate.
  The display policy matches the API used by `AndroidViewModuleNode` for visible
  text. Holder-group naming matches
  `GradleModuleSystem.getDisplayNameForModuleGroup:665`; sort identity matches
  the internal module name in `AndroidModuleNode.getSortKey:66`. Names already
  escaped or collision-suffixed by the importer are retained as supplied.
  `LinkedAndroidModuleGroupUtils.getHolderModule:61` falls back to the original
  module, and the DTO contract explicitly requires capturing that fallback name.
- All 20 supplementary test declarations were inspected, including unknown
  capture, source-set precedence, null equality, null/empty distinction,
  delimiters, holder fallback, distinct identities, Unicode/whitespace, and
  borrowed long names. Their names exactly match the attributed selection.
  These are source-derived regression cases, not ports of original test methods.

## Provenance and scope

All 172 frozen source entries matched their recorded SHA-256 at review and
again immediately before writing this report. All eight retained pinned source
files matched their recorded hashes and byte counts. Original attribution and
Apache 2.0 notice remain present. The 159 original tracked paths were checked:
158 remain byte-identical, and the sole changed original file is the one-line
additive `pub mod module_presentation;` export. The canonical parity matrix is
unchanged (SHA-256
`a8a9567ffa3c33762103f400fe626bb80dc1d2a51425a58ec761c3d88e755b21`).

The task plan and port descriptor accurately state the integration still
required: imported-name construction, qualified/collision naming, authoritative
Gradle getter capture, holder lookup, Kotlin import/capability, revision binding,
presentation publication, and the project panel. The existing tree adapter
rejects empty/multiline labels; the new policy preserves applicable empty-label
semantics and explicitly leaves adapter extension unported. The five original
generated-tree flows and Kotlin original tests remain unported/not_run, with
zero new canonical parity credit.

No Cargo, Gradle, compiler, app, SDK probe, cache, repository source, fixture,
matrix, main, or protected-branch mutation was performed in this review. Builds,
test execution, and actual app checks remain owned by the task/lead runtime
lease and must pass separately before task completion or protected merge.
